Mira: quick capture from this morning's load run — batch formation seems to prefer small microbatches for decode-heavy requests, causing kernel flips.

Mira: Short paste of profiler:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] model=redwood-gpt-xl seq=512 tokens=2306
batch_size=12 avg_tokens_per_batch=142
kernel: fused_attn_v2 selected for 1..8, matmul_fallback for >8
decode_latency_p95=310ms (long-decode-rate bucket)
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.79 for len_bucket=512-1024, 0.62 for 1024-2048
token_budget_target=256 (current), observed spillover=18%
```

Mira: raising because we saw a perf regression vs last week's run — throughput -8% on dedicated with quantized kernels.

Ashwin: Can you paste the kernel selection decision log? curious about threshold.

Mira: pasted below from runtime logs:
```
selected_kernel: if seq_tokens_per_request < 128 and decode_rate > 0.8 -> fused_attn_v2
else if seq_tokens_per_request < 512 -> fused_attn_v1
else -> matmul_fallback
```

Tam: hmm. decode_rate > 0.8 heuristic might be too aggressive; for long prompts decode_rate tends to drop during sampling due to temperature resamples. Might flip kernels mid-request causing cache thrash.

DevInfraBot: deploy 2026-03-17T09:15 rolling to canary: runtime/opt-batch-v2 :white_check_mark:

Ashwin: Proposal: add a queue-level token budget cap that biases kernel selection: if pending_tokens_in_queue > 4000 prefer matmul_fallback to avoid frequent kernel swaps. Also consider raising token_budget_target to 384 for decode-heavy cohorts.

Mira: noted. Also KV eviction shows increased writes during kernel flips — probably because different kernels use different KV layouts (observed in GC logs).

Tam: We should add a small experiment: 1) classify incoming requests into 3 cohorts: short(<128), mid(128-1024), long(>1024) by prompt len and maintain separate admission policies + token_budget targets. 2) instrument per-cohort kernel-stickiness metric.

Ashwin: +1. Metrics to track: kernel_switch_rate, kv_eviction_rate, p95_latency, throughput, tokens_per_second per cohort.

Mira: I'll push a prototype patch to batcher: change length buckets to [0,128,1024,inf], decode_rate bins [>1.2, 0.6-1.2, <0.6], and token budget defaults [128, 256, 384]. Will run A/B on canary.

Tam: For A/B, ensure we keep fallbacks: if kernel leads to OOM, fallback to matmul_fallback and emit evt tag kernel_fallback_oom.

Ashwin: Also add a low-cost flame graph exporter to console so SRE can link to it from runtime dashboard.

Mira: rolling experiment now. Will post results in ~30m. :rocket:

SRE Alex: FYI, running a background sweep to bump GPU affinity for canary to avoid noisy neighbors.

Mira: thanks — updated last run metrics in link: https://perf.redwood.internal/experiments/1936004321

Tam: ack
